jaravani.caption: Figure 2: The 32-station SAWS network (2016–2025), concen- trated in the eastern half of the country.

Figure 3: Extreme-hour against all-hour MAE per variable, relative to the best cell, one marker per model; subtitles give Table 5’s degradation range. Plotted on the interquartile mean, so CLCRN’s temperature point is not inflated by the divergent run.

Figure 4: Test MAE against forecast lead for each target vari- able, on log axes, with the persistence and climatology base- lines; means over ten seeds. Persistence’s diurnal sawtooth and the narrowing between architectures with lead are both visible.

Figure 5: Factorial read of the design: each panel plots a vari- able’s four cell means against the temporal axis, one line for the learned adaptive graph (AGCRN → MTGODE) and one for the geometric prior (CLCRN → STGODE); the subtitle gives the interaction. Interquartile means over ten seeds.

Figure 6: The December 2024 heatwave at Makatini, at 24- hour lead. Top: observed temperature and each model’s fore- cast, with hour- and calendar-relative exceedance shaded. Bottom: each detection model’s exceedance probability and its frozen decision threshold.

Figure 7: Left: every run’s MAE relative to the best cell, one point per seed (190 in total), by variable and model, with the divergent CLCRN temperature run marked. Right: the probability that a randomly drawn run of one model beats another, by target, with 95% intervals.

Figure 8: Per-station test MAE for one model per variable, named in each panel, one marker per station on the network map; subtitles give coastal against inland medians and a Mann–Whitney 𝑝 . The four models’ per-station error ranks correlate 0.98 to 1.00, so difficulty is shared.
